item.text:
Kishida’s 2024 economic policy looks mostly evidence-based and correction-oriented, with the strongest positives coming from his explicit use of wage data, BOJ guidance, recession/consumption diagnostics, targeted relief, and expert-led industrial policy. The main negatives are indirect: scandal-driven defensive politics, a still-heavy slogan frame around “New Form of Capitalism,” and a narrower migration-control line that can read as exclusionary rather than productivity-first.

**Accepted claims**
- **Japan downgrades view of economy on sluggish consumer spending** | Reuters | 2024-02-21 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375  
  Government downgraded its economic view and consumer-spending assessment after weak data, which is direct evidence of responding to evidence rather than denying the slowdown. `5B.7`

- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html  
  Kishida tied the year’s agenda to wage growth, reskilling, labor-market reform, infrastructure, capital investment, and cyber/legal preparation, which is a technocratic, correction-oriented policy mix rather than slogan-only governance. `5B.7, 5B.6, 5B.4`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida on the Bank of Japan Terminating Its Negative Interest Rate Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-03-19 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html  
  Kishida accepted the BOJ’s judgment that a price-wage virtuous cycle had been confirmed and emphasized continuity with the 2013 accord, which is strong evidence of evidence-based macro policy and respect for institutional correction. `5B.7, 5B.3`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-03-28 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/28kaiken.html  
  He paired the new budget with reserve-budget use for Noto recovery, incomes above price increases, and tougher enforcement of subcontract rules, showing practical correction of shocks and policy failures rather than denial. `5B.7, 5B.3, 5B.4`

- **Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Inauguration of the GX Promotion Organization** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-01 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01message.html  
  Kishida described a 150-trillion-yen GX investment roadmap, carbon-pricing tools, and emissions-trading frameworks, which is structured, institution-backed industrial policy rather than patronage or rhetorical politics. `5B.7, 5B.6, 5B.4`

- **Speech by Prime Minister Kishida at the Keidanren Summer Forum 2024** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-19 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/19forum.html  
  Kishida explicitly named productivity barriers, proposed digital and AI-enabled recombination of talent/resources, and paired that with “two-stage” support for households hurt by high prices, which reads as policy adjustment based on observed constraints. `5B.7, 5B.6`

- **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee, with popularity and budget on the line** | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362  
  This is mixed negative evidence: the funding scandal forced Kishida into defensive political management, suggesting short-term survival pressures were shaping the agenda alongside policy, not purely evidence-driven correction. `5B.7, 5B.5`

- **Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site, 2024 fact page** | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 | https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/  
  The tougher “illegal foreigners zero” line, including stricter screening and deportation enforcement, is a mixed negative signal because it looks more like exclusionary control than productivity-based policy design. `5B.7, 5B.4, 4B.7`

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Kishida’s economic policy was driven by outright denial, obvious patronage, or broad scapegoating.
- The negative record is mostly indirect: scandal-driven political defensiveness, repeated slogan framing around “New Form of Capitalism,” and the migrant-control line above.
